# {{name}}

> {{tagline}}

{{name}} is a free, open-source Mac app (MIT License; macOS {{minMacOS}} or later, Apple silicon and Intel) that you open on a second-hand Mac. In about two minutes it reports, in plain English, whether the Mac is Activation-Locked, managed by an organization (MDM) or assigned to a company in Apple Business or Apple School Manager, how worn the battery and SSD are, what the specs are, and whether it still gets macOS updates. Guided tests cover the keyboard, display, speakers, microphone, camera and trackpad, and it makes a shareable report card (PNG or PDF, serial masked).

- It runs only Apple's own tools, with fixed arguments: system_profiler, ioreg, sysctl, and profiles and fdesetup with "status". The company-assignment check is a command the user runs in Terminal (sudo /usr/bin/profiles show -type enrollment) and pastes back; the app never asks for a password.
- Read-only: it never deletes, moves or changes anything, never signs anyone out, and writes only a report the user saves.
- Offline: no network access, no analytics, no update check.
- It never helps bypass MDM or Activation Lock.
- It can't tell whether a Mac was reported lost or stolen, whether an Intel Mac has a firmware password, parts and repair history, or liquid damage.
- Download: {{baseURL}}/download/
- Source and support: https://github.com/{{releasesRepo}}
